title: Cost Lineage Ledger: per-request attribution, exportable cost slices & pricing UI patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a ‘Cost Lineage Ledger’ UI in the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level attribution across requests, shows lineage from route -> model -> variant -> tool calls, and provides exportable 'cost slice' artifacts (CSV/Parquet) for billing reconciliation and downstream analysis. Focus areas: (1) compact per-request breakdown cards for low-latency dashboards, (2) a ledger table mode for deep dives with sorting/filtering, (3) an export flow with schema/preview and pricing tier annotation, and (4) visual pricing pattern components to show per-unit bands and effective unit price after batching/caching policies.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype includes compact request cards + togglable ledger table view
Export flow present with selectable schema (CSV, Parquet), sample row preview, and column mapping for external billing systems
Pricing UI components illustrating: nominal unit price, effective unit price (post-batching/discounts), and per-slice breakdown
Design handoff tokens and accessibility notes included (contrast ratios, keyboard nav for table)
Design receives PM + Eng review sign-off and lists actionable implementation tickets

design_reviews: 2026-03-04 — Design crit with PM/Eng/Research: accepted ledger table layout, requested async export UX and explicit schema preview
2026-03-05 — Accessibility pass: contrast and keyboard navigation required for table controls
decisions: MVP will support CSV + Parquet exports via async jobs (server-side generation) to avoid UI timeouts
Default ledger view shows aggregated per-route totals for last 24h; user can expand to request-level cards
Pricing UI will always show both nominal and effective unit price; effective price calculation will include batching and cache credits computed server-side
tradeoffs: Table virtualization preferred over pagination for deep dives but increases client memory — opted for virtualization with row windowing to balance UX and memory
Showing per-token lineage increases row width and cognitive load; chosen approach is a collapsible 'lineage' column to keep compactness
Real-time per-request attribution is expensive at scale; ledger will default to aggregated buckets for >1M requests and provide sample slices for exports
next_steps: Create ENG tickets for: async export job, export schema contract, server-side effective-price computation, and ledger API endpoints (start/end cursors)
PM to confirm retention/backfill policy with billing team for export windows >90 days
Design to deliver final handoff (tokens, component variants, interaction specs) and update Figma with accepted changes
